name: Gold pink enamel
summary: A soft rose-pink overglaze enamel that colloidal gold makes. Painters mix it with white enamel to make a range of tints from deep rose to white.
how: Dissolve gold in acid and precipitate it with tin to make a purple powder.
Mix the powder with a lead glass frit and grind it to a fine paste.
Mix the pink with white enamel in different ratios to make tints.
Paint the tints on the fired glaze and fire again at 760 to 800 °C.

origin.note: Painters at the imperial kilns start to use an enamel of gold from Europe to make pink and its tints.

adoptions.via: Painters at Jingdezhen and in the palace workshops paint rose, flesh and petal tints on white porcelain in the Yongzheng and Qianlong years.
Sèvres painters fire a pink enamel of gold, later called rose Pompadour, on soft-paste porcelain.
